<transformation>
The input is treated as a tile map. The output is NxM times larger than the input (where the input is N rows x M cols). Each input cell at (BR, BC) with a non-zero value causes a copy of the full input to be placed in the corresponding NxM block of the output (at rows BR*N .. BR*N+N-1, cols BC*M .. BC*M+M-1). Each input cell with value 0 produces an all-zero block at that position.
</transformation>

<asp>
% Count distinct row/col indices — equals grid dimensions for 0-indexed inputs
n_rows(N) :- N = #count{R : input(R, _, _)}.
n_cols(N) :- N = #count{C : input(_, C, _)}.

% Output is NR*NR rows and NC*NC cols (input tiled by itself)
output_cell(R, C) :-
    input(BR, BC, _), input(DR, DC, _),
    n_rows(NR), n_cols(NC),
    R = BR*NR + DR, C = BC*NC + DC.

1 { output(R, C, Color) : color(Color) } 1 :- output_cell(R, C).

% Non-zero block: the sub-cell must equal the input value at the relative position
:- input(BR, BC, V), V != 0,
   input(DR, DC, TileColor),
   n_rows(NR), n_cols(NC),
   R = BR*NR + DR, C = BC*NC + DC,
   output(R, C, ActualColor), ActualColor != TileColor.

% Zero block: every sub-cell must be 0
:- input(BR, BC, 0),
   input(DR, DC, _),
   n_rows(NR), n_cols(NC),
   R = BR*NR + DR, C = BC*NC + DC,
   output(R, C, ActualColor), ActualColor != 0.
</asp>
</example_1>

<transformation>
The output is the same size as the input. Color-3 cells are unchanged. Non-3 cells (value 0) that are enclosed by color-3 walls — i.e., cannot reach the grid boundary via 4-connected movement through non-3 cells — are filled with color 4. All other non-3 cells remain 0.
</transformation>

<asp>
% Output has the same dimensions as the input
output_cell(R, C) :- input(R, C, _).
1 { output(R, C, Color) : color(Color) } 1 :- output_cell(R, C).

% Grid boundary coordinates
min_row(R) :- R = #min{Row : input(Row, _, _)}.
max_row(R) :- R = #max{Row : input(Row, _, _)}.
min_col(C) :- C = #min{Col : input(_, Col, _)}.
max_col(C) :- C = #max{Col : input(_, Col, _)}.

% 4-connected adjacency offsets
delta(0,1). delta(0,-1). delta(1,0). delta(-1,0).

% Non-3 cells on the grid boundary are reachable from outside
outside(R, C) :- input(R, C, V), V != 3, min_row(Rmin), R = Rmin.
outside(R, C) :- input(R, C, V), V != 3, max_row(Rmax), R = Rmax.
outside(R, C) :- input(R, C, V), V != 3, min_col(Cmin), C = Cmin.
outside(R, C) :- input(R, C, V), V != 3, max_col(Cmax), C = Cmax.

% Flood-fill outward through non-3 cells
outside(R2, C2) :-
    outside(R1, C1), delta(DR, DC),
    R2 = R1+DR, C2 = C1+DC,
    input(R2, C2, V), V != 3.

% Color-3 cells stay 3
:- input(R, C, 3), output(R, C, Color), Color != 3.

% Outside non-3 cells stay 0
:- outside(R, C), output(R, C, Color), Color != 0.

% Interior non-3 cells (enclosed by 3s, not reachable from boundary) become 4
:- input(R, C, 0), not outside(R, C), output(R, C, Color), Color != 4.
</asp>

% -------------------------------------------------
% Dimensions of the input grid
numRows(N) :- N = #count{R : input(R, _, _)}.
numCols(M) :- M = #count{C : input(_, C, _)}.

% Row and column indices (last row = N‑1, last col = M‑1)
maxRow(Rmax) :- Rmax = N-1.
maxCol(Cmax) :- Cmax = M-1.

% Colours that actually appear in the input
present(C) :- input(R, C2, V), V = C.

% Highest colour that appears – this will be the “wall” colour
maxColor(9) :- present(9).
maxColor(8) :- present(8), not present(9).
maxColor(7) :- present(7), not present(8), not present(9).
maxColor(6) :- present(6), not present(7), not present(8), not present(9).
maxColor(5) :- present(5), not present(6), not present(7), not present(8), not present(9).
maxColor(4) :- present(4), not present(5), not present(6), not present(7), not present(8), not present(9).
maxColor(3) :- present(3), not present(4), not present(5), not present(6), not present(7), not present(8), not present(9).
maxColor(2) :- present(2), not present(3), not present(4), not present(5), not present(6), not present(7), not present(8), not present(9).
maxColor(1) :- present(1), not present(2), not present(3), not present(4), not present(5), not present(6), not present(7), not present(8), not present(9).
maxColor(0) :- present(0), not present(1), not present(2), not present(3), not present(4), not present(5), not present(6), not present(7), not present(8), not present(9).

% The wall colour – the highest colour that is present (non‑zero)
wall(W) :- maxColor(W), W != 0.

% 4‑connected neighbourhood
delta(0,1). delta(0,-1). delta(1,0). delta(-1,0).

% Zero cells that lie on the border
borderZero(R,C) :- input(R,C,V), V = 0, R = 0.
borderZero(R,C) :- input(R,C,V), V = 0, R = maxRow.
borderZero(R,C) :- input(R,C,V), V = 0, C = 0.
borderZero(R,C) :- input(R,C,V), V = 0, C = maxCol.

% Zero cells reachable from the border through other zero cells only
reachable(R,C) :- borderZero(R,C).
reachable(R,C) :- reachable(R1,C1), delta(DR,DC), R = R1+DR, C = C1+DC, input(R,C,V), V = 0.

% -------------------------------------------------
% Output cell definition
% 1. Cells that are the wall colour stay unchanged
output_cell(R,C,Color) :- input(R,C,V), V = W, Color = V, wall(W).

% 2. Zero cells that can reach the border stay 0
output_cell(R,C,Color) :- input(R,C,V), V = 0, reachable(R,C), Color = 0.

% 3. Zero cells that are enclosed (not reachable) become the wall colour
output_cell(R,C,Color) :- input(R,C,V), V = 0, not reachable(R,C), Color = W, wall(W).

% 4. All other non‑zero non‑wall cells keep their original colour
output_cell(R,C,Color) :- input(R,C,V), V != 0, V != W, Color = V, wall(W).

% Exactly one output per cell
1 { output(R,C,Color) : color(Color) } 1 :- output_cell(R,C,Color).

n_rows(N) :- N = #count{R : input(R, _, _)}.

globalMax(M) :- M = #max { Color : input(_, _, Color) }.

% ----------  max colour in a particular row ----------
max_in_row(R, MaxR) :- MaxR = #max { Color : input(R, C, Color) }.

% max in the previous row (R‑1)
max_in_row_prev(R, MaxPrev) :- MaxPrev = #max { Color : input(R-1, C, Color) }.

% max in the next row (R+1)
max_in_row_next(R, MaxNext) :- MaxNext = #max { Color : input(R+1, C, Color) }.

% index of the last row (0‑based)
lastRow := #max { R : input(R, _, _) }.

% ----- block of rows with a row‑max smaller than the global maximum -----
% blockStart – first row of a block
blockStart(R) :- max_in_row(R, MaxR), MaxR < globalMax, (R = 0).

               max_in_row_prev(R, MaxPrev), MaxPrev != MaxR.

% blockEnd – last row of a block

blockEnd(R) :- max_in_row(R, MaxR), MaxR < globalMax,
               max_in_row_next(R, MaxNext), MaxNext != MaxR.

% first row of a block (unless the block reaches the bottom)

n_rows(N) :- N = #count{R : input(R, _, _)}.
n_cols(N) :- N = #count{C : input(_, C, _)}.

% Output is NR*NR rows and NC*NC cols (input tiled by itself)
output_cell(R, C) :-
    input(BR, BC, _), input(DR, DC, _),
    n_rows(NR), n_cols(NC),
    R = BR*NR + DR, C = BC*NC + DC.

1 { output(R, C, Color) : color(Color) } 1 :- output_cell(R, C).

% Non-zero block: the sub-cell must equal the input value at the relative position
:- input(BR, BC, V), V != 0,
   input(DR, DC, TileColor),

   R = BR*NR + DR, C = BC*NC + DC,
   output(R, C, ActualColor), ActualColor != TileColor.

% Zero block: every sub-cell must be 0
:- input(BR, BC, 0),
   input(DR, DC, _),
   n_rows(NR), n_cols(NC),
   R = BR*NR + DR, C = BC*NC + DC,

min_col(C) :- C = #min{Col : input(_, Col, _)}.
max_col(C) :- C = #max{Col : input(_, Col, _)}.

% 4-connected adjacency offsets
delta(0,1). delta(0,-1). delta(1,0). delta(-1,0).

% Non-3 cells on the grid boundary are reachable from outside
outside(R, C) :- input(R, C, V), V != 3, min_row(Rmin), R = Rmin.
outside(R, C) :- input(R, C, V), V != 3, max_row(Rmax), R = Rmax.
outside(R, C) :- input(R, C, V), V != 3, min_col(Cmin), C = Cmin.
outside(R, C) :- input(R, C, V), V != 3, max_col(Cmax), C = Cmax.

% Flood-fill outward through non-3 cells
outside(R2, C2) :-
    outside(R1, C1), delta(DR, DC),
    R2 = R1+DR, C2 = C1+DC,
    input(R2, C2, V), V != 3.

% Outside non-3 cells stay 0
:- outside(R, C), output(R, C, Color), Color != 0.

% Interior non-3 cells (enclosed by 3s, not reachable from boundary) become 4
:- input(R, C, 0), not outside(R, C), output(R, C, Color), Color != 4.

% compute number of rows and columns (max index)
max_row := #max {R : input(R, _, _)}.
max_col := #max {C : input(_, C, _)}.

% wall color (max color in input)
wall_color := #max {Color : input(_, _, Color)}.

% adjacency offsets
delta(0,1). delta(0,-1). delta(1,0). delta(-1,0).

% border cells that are not wall color
border(R,C) :- input(R,C,V), V != wall_color, (R = 0).
border(R,C) :- input(R,C,V), V != wall_color, (R = max_row).
border(R,C) :- input(R,C,V), V != wall_color, (C = 0).
border(R,C) :- input(R,C,V), V != wall_color, (C = max_col).

% flood fill through cells not wall
reachable(R,C) :- border(R,C).
reachable(R,C) :- reachable(R1,C1), delta(DR,DC), R = R1+DR, C = C1+DC,
                  input(R,C,V), V != wall_color.

% output cell assignment
output_cell(R,C,Color) :- input(R,C,V), V = wall_color, Color = V.
output_cell(R,C,Color) :- input(R,C,V), V != wall_color, reachable(R,C), Color = V.
output_cell(R,C,Color) :- input(R,C,V), V != wall_color, not reachable(R,C), Color = 0.

% final output
1 { output(R, C, Color) : color(Color) } 1 :- output_cell(R, C, Color).
